plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped blooms on sturdy stems above blue-green strap-like leaves. Late-season varieties are at their peak in early May across temperate gardens and the famous commercial fields of the Netherlands.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring to late spring (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Netherlands, northern Europe, North America, and temperate gardens worldwide; native to Central Asia
plants.funFact: In 17th-century Holland, tulip bulbs became so valuable during 'Tulip Mania' that a single rare bulb could cost more than a house.

plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A deciduous shrub producing dense, conical clusters of intensely fragrant tiny flowers. It thrives in cold-winter climates and typically reaches peak bloom in early to mid May in northern temperate regions.
plants.location: Northeastern United States, southern Canada, Europe; native to the Balkan Peninsula
plants.funFact: Lilacs can live for over 100 years and often persist at abandoned homesteads long after the buildings are gone.

plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: A vigorous twining woody vine that drapes pergolas, walls, and trees with long pendant racemes of fragrant pea-like flowers, often blooming before its leaves fully emerge.
plants.location: Native to China; cultivated in Japan, Europe, and the eastern and southern United States
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines twine counterclockwise, whereas the Japanese species Wisteria floribunda twines clockwise, and a single vine can live for well over a century.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall tropical and subtropical tree covered in trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers with fern-like foliage. In the Southern Hemisphere it is finishing its autumn display, while in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics such as parts of Mexico, Florida, and southern Asia it is beginning to bloom.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (May to June); spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; planted in Mexico, southern California, Florida, India, and parts of Africa
plants.funFact: Fallen jacaranda blossoms create purple carpets on streets, and in Pretoria, South Africa, it is known as the 'Jacaranda City' for its thousands of trees.
